messages:
olivia: Hey @people-ops  weird one. Hospital in Madrid is asking for an "insurance card" to clear a pre-op screening tomorrow. Dependent added last week, portal shows membership but no card. We don't have a printer here. Is a screen photo enough or do we need a formal letter?

toni (People Ops): A screenshot often passes for check-in but pre-op sometimes wants a signed proof on letterhead. Fastest options: 1) download the insurer's digital ID or print-to-PDF from the portal; 2) request an "expedited verification letter" from insurer (they can email/fax); 3) ask hospital to call insurer for phone verification. If you prefer we can request on your behalf  DM PII.

ruben: Had this with a surgery in Lisbon  hospital accepted an emailed PDF from the insurer and a verbal confirmation over the phone. They just needed member & group numbers plus policyholder name.

toni (People Ops): Quick how-to: Login to https://benefits.example.com -> Insurance -> Member ID. If page blocks download, do Print -> Save as PDF on your phone browser. If the PDF is missing the group number, call insurer and ask for an "expedited proof of coverage" and request they include member ID, group number, plan name and effective date. Ask them to email it to the hospital directly (get hospital email) or to you with a cc to the hospital.

olivia: Hospital wants a document on letterhead or a fax. They gave a fax number: +34-XXX-XXX-XXXX. Can insurer fax?

toni (People Ops): Many insurers can fax  when you call ask "Can you fax an expedited proof of coverage to [fax#]? We need member ID, group #, plan effective date, and policyholder name on letterhead for pre-op clearance." If insurer refuses, we can use broker to push or produce a company verification letter that confirms the dependent enrollment pending insurer confirmation (note: not a substitute for insurer letter, but sometimes accepted).

toni (People Ops): Sample call script: "Hello, I need an expedited proof of coverage faxed for dependent [name], DOB [mm/dd/yyyy], member ID [if known]. Our hospital needs it for pre-operative clearance tomorrow. Please include member ID, group number, plan name, effective date, and policyholder's name. Can you fax it to [fax#] and/or email to [email]?"

olivia: DMing you the dependent details now.

people-ops-bot: Enrollment & expedite form: https://hr.example.com/dependents -> "Expedited proof request". Also claims guide: https://hr.example.com/claims/foreign-providers.

ruben: For the eventual claim: get itemized pre-op labs and procedure codes, provider name + NPI if available, and a stamped invoice. Hospitals often give a "patient report" with codes after the visit — keep that.

olivia: Thanks — fax went through from insurer and hospital accepted the faxed letter. Pre-op cleared! Appreciate the rapid help :tada:
